raw_text:
Below is a gentle, progressive 12‑week postpartum return programme designed for a client 4 weeks post uncomplicated C‑section, currently cleared only for light activity (walking), no direct abdominal work or heavy lifting until her 6‑week check. The plan respects tissue healing, emphasizes breathing, pelvic floor, posture, circulation, and gradual reintroduction of load-bearing and core work after medical re-clearance. It’s organized into four phases with week-by-week details. Always defer to her OB/midwife if any symptoms arise (see red flags at the end).

General guidelines
- Session frequency and duration: Start with short, frequent bouts. Quality over quantity. Stop before fatigue alters form.
- Intensity: Keep effort light to moderate (RPE 2–5/10) in Phases 1–2. Progress only if symptom-free.
- Breathing: Prioritize diaphragmatic breathing with 360° rib expansion and gentle pelvic floor coordination on exhales.
- Core rule: No doming/coning of the abdominal wall, incision discomfort, pelvic heaviness/pressure, urinary leakage, or increased bleeding. Regress if present.
- Incision care: Avoid pressure on the scar until comfortable; support with hands or a pillow when coughing/sneezing.
- Pelvic floor: Gentle, submaximal contractions; avoid bearing down. Emphasize full relaxation between reps.

Equipment: yoga mat; a chair; later, household items for light resistance (water bottles, light backpack) if appropriate and cleared.

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2 of this plan; client is 4–6 weeks postpartum): Restore breath, gentle pelvic floor, circulation, posture; walking only. No direct abdominal loading. Await 6‑week check.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 3–4; 6–8 weeks postpartum): If medically re-cleared at 6‑week check, add very low-load foundational strength, gentle core reactivation, progressive walking.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 5–8; 8–12 weeks postpartum): Build full-body strength endurance, anti-rotation core, balance, tempo control. Introduce light external load from household items as tolerated.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 9–12; 12–16 weeks postpartum): Progress to moderate strength, low-impact conditioning, integrated core with gradual challenge.

Session structure (for most sessions after Week 2)
1) Check-in: symptoms, incision comfort, pelvic floor status
2) Breath/pelvic floor activation and mobility (5–10 min)
3) Strength and motor control (10–25 min)
4) Cooldown and recovery (3–5 min)
Walking is programmed separately.

PHASE 1: Weeks 1–2 (Client at 4–6 weeks postpartum)
Goal: Reconnect breath/pelvic floor, promote healing and circulation, maintain posture, and establish routine. No direct ab work. Keep everything pain-free and submax.

Weekly schedule
- 4–6 days/week: Walking
- 4 days/week: Gentle restorative session (10–20 min)
- Daily: Scar desensitization only if incision is fully closed and non-tender (light touch around, not on, scar), posture resets, breath work

Walking (both weeks)
- Frequency: 4–6 days/week
- Duration: Start 10–20 min/day at easy pace; break into 5–10 min bouts if needed
- Progression: Add 2–5 min per walk every few days if symptom-free; aim for 20–30 min by end of Week 2
- Monitor: No pelvic heaviness, increased bleeding, or incision pulling

Restorative sessions (4x/week)
A. Breathing and pelvic floor (perform supine with head elevated or sidelying if more comfortable)
- 360° diaphragmatic breathing: 5 breaths x 2–3 sets
- Pelvic floor “exhale and lift” (30–50% effort) with full release on inhale: 5 reps x 2 sets
- Long holds: 3–4 seconds lift, 6–8 seconds release x 3 reps
- Add “open mouth sigh” to encourage relaxation if gripping

B. Mobility/posture
- Cat-cow range (small, pain-free): 6–8 reps
- Seated thoracic rotation (hands across chest): 6–8/side
- Supported chest opener at wall or doorway: 30–45 sec
- Ankle pumps/circles: 10/side

C. Gentle lower-limb and glute activation (no strain on abs)
- Seated marching (tiny range): 8–10/side x 2
- Sidelying clamshells (light): 8–10/side x 2
- Sit-to-stand from a high chair (arms assist as needed): 6–8 x 2
- Standing heel raises: 8–10 x 2
- Quadruped rock-backs (small range, neutral spine, stop if pressure at scar): 6–8

Notes
- Avoid planks, crunches, curl-ups, heavy lifting, or Valsalva.
- If any symptom occurs, reduce volume or regress.

6‑WEEK CHECK
- Proceed to Phase 2 only after OB/midwife re-clearance for increased activity and gentle core work. If not yet cleared, repeat Week 2 until cleared.

PHASE 2: Weeks 3–4 (6–8 weeks postpartum, post-clearance)
Goal: Reintroduce foundational strength and gentle core reactivation while maintaining symptom-free walking.

Weekly schedule
- Walking: 5 days/week
- Strength/mobility sessions: 3 days/week (non-consecutive), 25–35 min
- Optional recovery day: 1–2 light restorative breath/mobility sessions

Walking
- 25–35 min at easy-moderate pace; include 2–3 x 2–3 min brisk segments if symptom-free

Sessions (3x/week)
A. Prep (5–7 min)
- 360° breathing with pelvic floor coordination: 5 breaths x 2
- Supine heel slides with exhale-engage (hand on belly to monitor for doming): 6–8/side x 2
- Dead bug arms only (legs bent, feet down): 6–8/side x 2

B. Strength/motor control (2–3 sets each, rest 45–60s, RPE 3–5)
- Sit-to-stand (controlled, no breath-hold): 8–10
- Wall push-ups: 8–10
- Hip hinge patterning with dowel/broom (no load): 8–10
- Sidelying clamshells or bandless lateral abduction: 10–12/side
- Bird-dog (arms only or legs only to start): 5–6/side; progress to full if no coning
- Standing band pull-aparts with very light resistance or towel isometrics: 10–12

C. Core integration (gentle)
- Supine marching (tabletop optional if symptom-free): 5–8/side x 1–2 sets
- Pallof press isometric with light band or hands pressing into each other at chest height: 10–15s x 3
- Finish with child’s pose or side-lying breathing: 5 breaths x 2

PHASE 3: Weeks 5–8 (8–12 weeks postpartum)
Goal: Build strength endurance and dynamic control. Introduce light external load via household items if comfortable.

Weekly schedule
- Walking or low-impact cardio: 5–6 days/week; 30–40 min total; include 4–6 x 1–2 min brisk intervals
- Strength sessions: 3 days/week; 30–40 min

Sessions (A/B alternating)

Session A
1) Prep
- Breathing reset + pelvic floor: 5 breaths
- Dead bug progression (opposite arm/leg taps, small range): 6–8/side x 2

2) Strength (2–3 sets, RPE 4–6)
- Squat to chair (add light load like 1–3 kg backpack at chest if tolerated): 8–12
- Elevated push-up (countertop): 8–12
- Hip hinge to mini Romanian deadlift with light load (backpack or water jugs): 8–10
- Step-ups to low step (controlled): 6–8/side
- Bird-dog (full): 6–8/side
- Standing row with band or towel-isometric row against sturdy object: 10–12

3) Core/conditioning finisher (low impact)
- Standing Pallof press: 8–10/side x 2
- Farmer carry light (two water bottles), tall posture, easy pace: 30–45s x 2

Session B
1) Prep
- Side-lying rib expansion breathing: 5 breaths/side
- Glute bridge (small lift, ribs down): 8–10 x 2

2) Strength (2–3 sets, RPE 4–6)
- Reverse lunges to split-stance (hold chair for balance): 6–8/side
- One-arm supported row (light load): 10–12/side
- Overhead press partial range with very light load (water bottle), exhale through press: 8–10
- Lateral step-outs (mini side squat): 8–10/side
- Tall-kneeling or half-kneeling anti-rotation press (band or hands): 8–10/side

3) Core control
- Heel taps from tabletop (only if zero doming): 6–8/side x 2
- Side plank modified (knees down) or wall side plank isometric: 10–20s/side x 2

PHASE 4: Weeks 9–12 (12–16 weeks postpartum)
Goal: Progress to moderate strength, integrated core, and low-impact conditioning. Maintain symptom monitoring.

Weekly schedule
- Conditioning: 2 days/week brisk intervals (e.g., walk 5 min easy + 6–8 x 1–2 min brisk, 1–2 min easy + cool down)
- Steady walks: 2–3 additional days/week, 30–45 min
- Strength: 3 days/week; 35–45 min

Strength sessions (A/B/C rotating)

Session A
- Prep: Breath + banded or towel lat prayer stretch: 5 breaths
- Goblet squat with moderate light (4–8 kg if available; otherwise heavier backpack): 6–10 x 3
- Elevated push-up (lower the elevation as tolerated): 6–10 x 3
- Hip hinge: RDL with light-moderate load: 8–10 x 3
- Step-up or split squat: 6–8/side x 3
- Dead bug or hollow brace variations at low intensity: 6–8/side x 2
- Carry: Suitcase carry light-moderate: 20–40m/side x 2

Session B
- Prep: Glute bridge with 2–3s pause: 8–10 x 2
- One-arm row (moderate light): 8–12/side x 3
- Overhead press (very light to light, strict, exhale): 6–10 x 3
- Lateral lunge to box or step touch: 6–8/side x 3
- Modified side plank with top-leg straight (progress time): 15–30s/side x 2–3
- Pallof press or anti-rotation hold: 8–12/side x 2–3

Session C
- Prep: Diaphragm + pelvic floor coordination
- Tempo squat (3s down, 1s up): 6–8 x 3
- Hip bridge march (slow): 6–8/side x 2–3
- Bent-over T/Y shoulder raises (no/very light load): 8–12 each x 2–3
- Reverse lunge or step-back to balance: 6–8/side x 3
- Bear position holds (knees hovering 1–2 inches, only if no symptoms): 10–20s x 2–3

Progression rules across Phases 2–4
- Increase reps first, then sets, then lower support/elevation, then load.
- Keep RPE ≤6 most days; brief RPE 7 sets in Weeks 11–12 if symptom-free.
- Maintain diaphragmatic breathing; avoid breath-holding on effort.
- Core check each session: watch for doming, tugging at scar, pelvic heaviness, incontinence, or back pain.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep: Nap when possible; prioritize total rest. Training volume flexes with sleep quality.
- Hydration: ~2–3 L/day, more if breastfeeding; electrolytes as needed.
- Nutrition: Aim for protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day, colorful produce, whole grains, healthy fats. If breastfeeding, add ~300–500 kcal/day and ensure calcium, iodine, choline, DHA, iron as appropriate. Refer to a dietitian if unsure.
- Bowel/bladder: Avoid straining; use breathing (“exhale on effort”) for bowel movements. Consider a stool to elevate feet.
- Scar care: Once fully healed per provider, gentle scar mobilization 2–3 min/day; stop if painful.
- Posture breaks: Short movement breaks every 45–60 min.

When to pause and refer back to provider
- Increased vaginal bleeding or change back to bright red after exercise
- Incision redness, warmth, discharge, or opening
- Pelvic heaviness/pressure, bulging, or pain suggestive of prolapse
- Urinary or fecal incontinence; pain with bowel movements
- Persistent low back, pelvic, or hip pain
- Abdominal doming/coning that doesn’t resolve with cueing
- Dizziness, chest pain, calf pain/swelling
Consider referral to a pelvic health physical therapist for individualized assessment, scar mobilization guidance, diastasis assessment, and pelvic floor rehab.

Notes for the trainer
- Keep communication open; adjust sets/reps daily for energy and symptoms.
- If equipment becomes available (mini-bands, light dumbbells), we can scale more precisely.
- This is a general plan; always individualize to her presentation, healing, and medical guidance.
